name: Lazarus Group – APT Threat Map
description: Técnicas de Lazarus Group com cobertura do catálogo (score 3=regra, 2=parcial, 1=lacuna)

techniques.comment: Lazarus Group malware also uses a unique form of communication encryption known as FakeTLS that mimics TLS but uses a different encryption method, potentially evading SSL traffic inspection/decryption. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has collected data and files from compromised networks. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware SierraAlfa sends data to one of the hard-coded C2 servers chosen at random, and if the transmission fails, chooses a new C2 server to attempt the transmission again. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware IndiaIndia obtains and sends to its C2 server the title of the window for each running process. The KilaAlfa keylogger also reports the title of the window in the foreground. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware IndiaIndia checks Registry keys within HKCU and HKLM to determine if certain applications are present, including SecureCRT, Terminal Services, RealVNC, TightVNC, UltraVNC, Radmin, mRemote, TeamViewer, FileZilla, pcAnyware, and Remote Desktop. Another Lazarus Group malware sample checks for the presence of the following Registry… | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware IndiaIndia obtains and sends to its C2 server information about the first network interface card’s configuration, including IP address, gateways, subnet mask, DHCP information, and whether WINS is available. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware SierraCharlie uses RDP for propagation. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware SierraAlfa accesses the `ADMIN$` share via SMB to conduct lateral movement. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group used SSH and the PuTTy PSCP utility to gain access to a restricted segment of a compromised network. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used a custom hashing method to resolve APIs used in shellcode. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has distributed malicious payloads embedded in PNG files. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group has used multiple types of encryption and encoding for their payloads, including AES, Caracachs, RC4, XOR, Base64, and other tricks such as creating aliases in code for Native API function names. | cobertura: regra
Various Lazarus Group malware enumerates logged-on users. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has renamed system utilities such as `wscript.exe` and `mshta.exe`. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used a scheduled task named `SRCheck` to mask the execution of a malicious .dll. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has renamed malicious code to disguise it as Microsoft's narrator and other legitimate files. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has exfiltrated data and files over a C2 channel through its various tools and malware. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used nmap from a router VM to scan ports on systems within the restricted segment of an enterprise network. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used WMIC for discovery as well as to execute payloads for persistence and lateral movement. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware SierraBravo-Two generates an email message via SMTP containing information about newly infected victims. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used `net use` to identify and establish a network connection with a remote host. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used `schtasks` for persistence including through the periodic execution of a remote XSL script or a dropped VBS payload. | cobertura: regra
A Lazarus Group malware sample performs reflective DLL injection. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware KiloAlfa contains keylogging functionality. | cobertura: regra

Several Lazarus Group malware families gather a list of running processes on a victim system and send it to their C2 server. A Destover-like variant used by Lazarus Group also gathers process times. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used PowerShell to execute commands and malicious code. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware uses cmd.exe to execute commands on a compromised host. A Destover-like variant used by Lazarus Group uses a batch file mechanism to delete its binaries from the system. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used VBA and embedded macros in Word documents to execute malicious code. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has restored malicious KernelCallbackTable code to its original state after the process execution flow has been hijacked. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has routinely deleted log files on a compromised router, including automatic log deletion through the use of the logrotate utility. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware has deleted files in various ways, including "suicide scripts" to delete malware binaries from the victim. Lazarus Group also uses secure file deletion to delete files from the victim. | cobertura: regra

Several Lazarus Group malware families use timestomping, including modifying the last write timestamp of a specified Registry key to a random date, as well as copying the timestamp for legitimate .exe files (such as calc.exe or mspaint.exe) to its dropped files. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has conducted C2 over HTTP and HTTPS. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware IndiaIndia saves information gathered about the victim to a file that is saved in the %TEMP% directory, then compressed, encrypted, and uploaded to a C2 server. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used administrator credentials to gain access to restricted network segments. | cobertura: regra
Several Lazarus Group malware families collect information on the type and version of the victim OS, as well as the victim computer name and CPU information. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware can use a common function to identify target files by their extension, and some also enumerate files and directories, including a Destover-like variant that lists files and gathers information for all drives. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used a compromised router to serve as a proxy between a victim network's corporate and restricted segments. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used multiple proxies to obfuscate network traffic from victims. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware WhiskeyDelta-Two contains a function that attempts to rename the administrator’s account. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used GitHub as C2, pulling hosted image payloads then committing command execution output to files in specific directories. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used multi-stage malware components that inject later stages into separate processes. | cobertura: parcial (ASR/D3FEND)
Lazarus Group has downloaded files, malware, and tools from its C2 onto a compromised host. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group has used the Windows API `ObtainUserAgentString` to obtain the User-Agent from a compromised host to connect to a C2 server. Lazarus Group has also used various, often lesser known, functions to perform various types of Discovery and Process Injection. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group malware attempts to connect to Windows shares for lateral movement by using a generated list of usernames, which center around permutations of the username Administrator, and weak passwords. | cobertura: regra
A Destover-like implant used by Lazarus Group can obtain the current system time and send it to the C2 server. | cobertura: regra
A Lazarus Group malware sample encodes data with base64. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group has used shellcode within macros to decrypt and manually map DLLs and shellcode into memory at runtime. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group delivered RATANKBA and other malicious code to victims via a compromised legitimate website. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group persistence mechanisms have used `forfiles.exe` to execute .htm files. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has exploited Adobe Flash vulnerability CVE-2018-4878 for execution. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has attempted to get users to launch a malicious Microsoft Word attachment delivered via a spearphishing email. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group lnk files used for persistence have abused the Windows Update Client (`wuauclt.exe`) to execute a malicious DLL. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used `mshta.exe` to execute HTML pages downloaded by initial access documents. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used rundll32 to execute malicious payloads on a compromised host. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used a custom secure delete function to overwrite file contents with data from heap memory. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has stopped the MSExchangeIS service to render Exchange contents inaccessible to users. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group replaced the background wallpaper of systems with a threatening image after rendering the system unbootable with a Disk Structure Wipe. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has rebooted systems after destroying files and wiping the MBR on infected systems. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware WhiskeyAlfa-Three modifies sector 0 of the Master Boot Record (MBR) to ensure that the malware will persist even if a victim machine shuts down. | cobertura: regra
Several Lazarus Group malware families install themselves as new services. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has maintained persistence by loading malicious code into a startup folder or by adding a Registry Run key. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware has maintained persistence on a system by creating a LNK shortcut in the user’s Startup folder. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has digitally signed malware and utilities to evade detection. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group executed Responder using the command `[Responder file path] -i [IP address] -rPv` on a compromised host to harvest credentials and move laterally. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has compressed exfiltrated data with RAR and used RomeoDelta malware to archive specified directories in .zip format, encrypt the .zip file, and upload it to C2. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware IndiaIndia saves information gathered about the victim to a file that is compressed with Zlib, encrypted, and uploaded to a C2 server. | cobertura: regra
A Lazarus Group malware sample encrypts data using a simple byte based XOR operation prior to exfiltration. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group has used malware like WhiskeyAlfa to overwrite the first 64MB of every drive with a mix of static and random buffers. A similar process is then used to wipe content in logical drives and, finally, attempt to wipe every byte of every sector on every drive. WhiskeyBravo can be used to overwrite the first 4.9MB of physical drives. WhiskeyDelta… | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group malware SHARPKNOT overwrites and deletes the Master Boot Record (MBR) on the victim's machine and has possessed MBR wiper malware since at least 2009. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used a VBA Macro to set its file attributes to System and Hidden and has named files with a dot prefix to hide them from the Finder application. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has targeted victims with spearphishing emails containing malicious Microsoft Word documents. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has sent malicious links to victims via email. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has used social media platforms, including LinkedIn and Twitter, to send spearphishing messages. | cobertura: regra
Some Lazarus Group malware uses a list of ordered port numbers to choose a port for C2 traffic, creating port-protocol mismatches. | cobertura: regra

Several Lazarus Group malware families encrypt C2 traffic using custom code that uses XOR with an ADD operation and XOR with a SUB operation. Another Lazarus Group malware sample XORs C2 traffic. Other Lazarus Group malware uses Caracachs encryption to encrypt C2 payloads. Lazarus Group has also used AES to encrypt C2 traffic. | cobertura: regra

Lazarus Group has replaced `win_fw.dll`, an internal component that is executed during IDA Pro installation, with a malicious DLL to download and execute a payload. Lazarus Group utilized DLL side-loading to execute malicious payloads through abuse of the legitimate processes `wsmprovhost.exe` and `dfrgui.exe`. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has abused the `KernelCallbackTable` to hijack process control flow and execute shellcode. | cobertura: regra
Lazarus Group has acquired domains related to their campaigns to act as distribution points and C2 channels. | cobertura: lacuna
Lazarus Group has hosted malicious downloads on Github. | cobertura: lacuna

Lazarus Group has created new Twitter accounts to conduct social engineering against potential victims. | cobertura: lacuna
Lazarus Group has created new email accounts for spearphishing operations. | cobertura: lacuna
Lazarus Group has developed custom malware for use in their operations. | cobertura: regra
